name: Postman
scope_notes: Cloud SaaS; admin key management, service accounts, SCIM and audit logs need Enterprise (SSO also on Team with Simple Security add-on).

controls.name: Allow anyone in your team to generate API keys
controls.what: Turn off to stop users creating new Postman API keys.
controls.setting: Organization > Postman Keys > API Key Settings

controls.name: Set expiry for API keys
controls.what: Org-wide expiry for all keys, overriding user settings.
controls.setting: Organization > Postman Keys > API Key Settings

controls.name: Revoke (API key management dashboard)
controls.what: Revoke single or selected keys; owner is emailed.

controls.name: Revoke all API keys generated by your team
controls.what: Revoke every Postman API key the org created.
controls.setting: Organization > Postman Keys > API Key Settings

controls.name: Auto revoke exposed Postman API keys
controls.what: Auto-revoke keys the Secret Scanner finds in public Postman resources, GitHub or GitLab.
controls.setting: Organization > Postman Keys > API Key Settings

controls.name: Delete API key (account settings)
controls.what: Key owner can regenerate or delete their own key.

controls.name: Service account API key management
controls.what: Admins create, rotate, revoke or delete service account keys and set key expiry.

controls.name: Service account roles
controls.what: Service account access follows the org, team and workspace roles assigned to it.
controls.setting: Service Accounts > Assigned teams / Assigned workspaces

controls.name: SCIM API key turn on/off, regenerate, delete
controls.what: Disable, replace or delete a service-account-owned SCIM key.

controls.name: Allow creation of Collection Access Keys
controls.what: Turn off to stop members creating collection access keys.

controls.name: Revoke All Keys (collection access keys)
controls.what: Delete one or all team collection access keys; permanent.
controls.setting: Manage public elements > Collection Access Keys; DELETE /collection-access-keys/{keyId}

controls.name: Revoke an OAuth Token
controls.what: Revoke an OAuth access token immediately.

controls.name: Service account management restricted to Admin or Super Admin
controls.what: Only Admins and Super Admins can create service accounts and generate their API keys.

no_control.what: Service account short-lived token expiration cannot be configured.

controls_unknown: Any IP allowlisting for Postman API keys or the Postman API (none found in docs).
Whether API keys or service account tokens are blocked by SSO-only enforcement or IdP conditional access; docs do not say.
Whether revoking a service account API key invalidates already-issued short-lived tokens.
Whether removing or SCIM-deactivating a user revokes their Postman API keys.
Default and allowed expiry values for user API keys and SCIM keys.
Exact audit action codes for service account key events and collection access key create/delete.
Whether Postman API read calls (GET /collections, /workspaces, etc.) appear in audit logs.
How OAuth client_credentials clients (installationAuthId) are registered and administered.
Documented prefix for user Postman API keys (OAuth token example shows PMAK-XXX; not stated for API keys).

authentication.summary: User generates a key in Account settings > API keys and sends it in the X-API-Key header. It carries everything the user can access.

federation.details: No workload identity federation documented for this credential.

ip_restriction.boundary: No Postman doc found describing IP allowlisting for API keys or the Postman API.

lifetime.summary: User-set expiry; Enterprise admins can force an org expiry

renewal.expiry_basis: Expiry set by user or org policy; keys can be revoked for inactivity past expiry
renewal.summary: Regenerate or create a new key

administration.summary: Enterprise admins can block creation, force expiry, see last use, revoke one/many/all, and auto-revoke keys the Secret Scanner finds exposed.
administration.conditions: Enterprise plan; Admin or Super Admin

inventory.details: Enterprise Admins see every org-created Postman API key in the Postman API key management dashboard (Organization > Postman Keys).

token_format.notes: Prefix not stated for user API keys; audit logs show a masked identifier like 6948d*****.

federation.details: No workload identity federation documented for this credential.

ip_restriction.boundary: No Postman doc found describing IP allowlisting for API keys or the Postman API.

lifetime.summary: Token TTL fixed (value not stated); API key expiry configurable

renewal.expiry_basis: Long-lived key re-exchanged for new short-lived tokens
renewal.summary: Rotate by creating a second key, then revoking the old one

administration.summary: Admins create accounts, assign org/team/workspace roles, create, rotate, revoke or delete keys, and see last use.
administration.conditions: Enterprise plan; Admin or Super Admin

offboard.details: System service accounts are non-human identities, not tied to a user.

inventory.details: Admins see all system service accounts and their active credentials on the Service Accounts page.

expiry.ui: Profile > team/organization > Service Accounts > select account > view each API key's expiration (access token TTL is fixed, not configurable)

authentication.summary: Bearer key in the Authorization header for /scim/v2 endpoints only. Owned by an Admin/Super Admin user or by a system service account.

renewal.summary: Regenerate; old key can stay active during switch

administration.summary: Generated under Organization settings > Authentication after SSO and SCIM are on. Service-account keys can be renamed, turned off, regenerated, deleted. Power follows owner role.

offboard.details: Docs imply a SCIM key owned by an Admin stops working when that Admin leaves; keys owned by a service account keep working.

inventory.details: SCIM keys are managed in Organization settings (Authentication) and service-account-owned keys are listed on the service account; no doc describes one org-wide list.

offboard.ui: Remove the owning Admin from the team (Admin/Org Manager/Super Admin only), or deactivate via IdP SCIM; keys owned by a service account are unaffected

authentication.summary: Client application posts client ID/secret (Basic) plus installationAuthId and a signed JWT to POST /oauth2/token and gets a Bearer token. Docs do not say how clients are registered.

federation.details: Signed JWT assertion is required but issuer/trust setup is not documented.

renewal.summary: Request a new token with client credentials

administration.summary: Tokens can be revoked via POST /oauth2/token/revoke. No admin console for these clients found.

offboard.details: Client credentials tokens are issued to a client application for backend services or bots, not to a user.
